solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The cost of keeping horses makes you irritable

definitions.meaning: the fee paid to a stable for keeping and feeding someone's horse
..., like liverish, is an old word for bad-tempered, from a disordered liver

explanation.surface: A grumble that the bills for stabling horses put you in a foul mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Livery stables charge a keeping fee, and a liverish person is short-tempered: two separate senses of one word.

clue.text: Key storage area

parts.note: read as a crucial place for storage, but also a place you secure with a key, as at a gym or school

explanation.definitionFit: A locker is a small cupboard secured with a key for storing belongings.

clue.text: Put a coat on and disappeared around the end of December

indicators.note: the word for disappeared goes round the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: vanished means disappeared

indicators.note: only the closing letter of December is taken

explanation.surface: Someone put on a coat and vanished around late December.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put a coat on' suggests dressing for winter; it means a coat of varnish.
explanation.definitionFit: To varnish something is to apply a coat of protective finish.

clue.text: Searching unimportant — wasting time

indicators.note: the word for time is wasted, so that letter is lost from the word

parts.note: trifling means unimportant

explanation.surface: Searching for trivia is a waste of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Rifling through something is searching it hastily.

clue.text: What you need is liquid preparation

definitions.meaning: the thing that solves your problem, the answer you are after
a substance dissolved in a liquid, as a chemist mixes it

explanation.surface: A pharmacist's advice that a liquid remedy is just what you require.
explanation.definitionFit: A solution is both the answer to a problem and a mixture dissolved in liquid.

clue.text: One's played for nothing in order …

indicators.note: the zero goes inside the honour

parts.note: OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is an honour
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone plays for no fee, carried over in an ellipsis to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboe is a woodwind instrument, something that is played.

clue.text: …to experience initial excitement in new ground

indicators.note: the opening letter sits inside the rearranged letters
the word ground is made new, rearranged
only the opening letter of excitement is used

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: to feel a first thrill on fresh ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges GROUND to UNDRGO, and E from 'initial excitement' goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something is to experience or go through it.

clue.text: Useless writer's put up in it

indicators.note: the turned word goes inside the other
in a down clue, put up means written bottom to top, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a pen is a writer's tool

explanation.surface: A writer's work is put in it, but it is useless.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy and ineffective, useless at something.

clue.text: Talked of new leader — poorly treated

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word new is taken
treated is handled poorly, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: People gossiped about a new boss who treated staff badly.
explanation.definitionFit: To natter is to chat idly, so nattered means talked.

clue.text: One holds one's drink, with a right to enter greasy spoon

indicators.note: the clue says these letters go into the eating place, so they sit inside it

parts.note: a greasy spoon is a cheap café serving fried food

explanation.surface: Someone at a cheap café who can hold their drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One holds one's drink' reads as a person with a strong head, but it describes a vessel that holds a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is a glass jug or flask for serving wine or water, so it holds a drink.

clue.text: Measures against viral infection result in loss of nerve

indicators.note: one piece set against or beside the other, the infection coming first

parts.note: a cold is a common virus infection
feet are units of length

explanation.surface: Precautions against a virus end up making someone lose their nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: To get cold feet is an idiom for losing your nerve before something.

clue.text: Went in and made a record

definitions.meaning: to enter a room is to go in
to enter details is to write them in a log

explanation.surface: Someone came in and logged the fact.
explanation.definitionFit: Entered means both came in and recorded in a book or register.

clue.text: Is it done for changing issues?

indicators.note: the letters of these three words are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about whether something is finished for the sake of alteration.
explanation.definitionFit: Editions of a newspaper or magazine are its issues, each one printed run.

clue.text: Squirm, seeing legal document served by ambassador

indicators.note: the document comes first, delivered by the envoy who follows it

parts.note: a writ is a written court order
HE stands for His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: Someone wriggles uncomfortably on being handed a writ by a diplomat.
explanation.walkthrough: An ambassador is addressed as His Excellency, abbreviated HE.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist and squirm, as in pain or discomfort.

clue.text: Saw last of essays to be summarised

indicators.note: only the closing letter of essays is taken

parts.note: a potted history is a summarised one

explanation.surface: A teacher looks at the last essay to be summed up.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to see it, so spotted means saw.

clue.text: On drugs and volatile — it could be the cause of an outburst

definitions.text: it could be the cause of an outburst

parts.note: someone on drugs is high
volatile means liable to explode

explanation.surface: A description of someone intoxicated and hot-tempered, liable to blow up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a person's outburst of temper; the definition means a bomb's blast.
explanation.definitionFit: A powerful bomb material causes a violent blast, a literal outburst.

clue.text: Sun in race for circulation and coverage

indicators.note: the letters circulate, moved round into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper, the Sun, races for higher sales and wider coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid; 'circulation' looks like newspaper sales but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance gives cover, so an insurance policy is coverage against loss.

clue.text: Delights confronting credit controller in aircraft

indicators.note: the first word stands facing the second, ahead of it

parts.note: joys are delights
tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A credit controller is delighted, on a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: Buying 'on tick' is British slang for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A joystick is the control lever used to steer an aircraft.

clue.text: Apocryphal stories from men who are divorced

definitions.meaning: superstitious or untrue beliefs handed down as folk wisdom
read literally, stories told by divorced men about their former spouses

explanation.surface: A suggestion that dubious stories come from divorced men.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names traditional beliefs that are untrue, and divorced men might well tell tales of their exes.

clue.text: One starts to make progress concerning such painting

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the opening letters of the two words are taken

parts.note: as to means concerning or about

explanation.surface: An artist begins to make headway with a particular style of painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is painting with paint laid on thickly, so the brush strokes stand out.

clue.text: Drink put on part of plane for flyer

indicators.note: in a down clue, the drink is placed on top of the next piece

parts.note: to lap is to drink, as a cat does
a wing is part of an aeroplane

explanation.surface: A drink spilt on an aircraft's wing for a passenger.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapwing is a bird, and birds are flyers.

clue.text: Early goals at start — rest troubled wingers

indicators.note: the opening letters of the two words are taken
rest is troubled, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Early goals unsettle the team's wide players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges REST to RETS; wingers in football are wide players, but here they are birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Egrets are herons, birds with wings, so wingers in a playful sense.

clue.text: Finally address grave-sounding screenplay

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word address is taken
the word for a burial place is said aloud and written as it is pronounced

parts.note: a crypt is an underground burial vault

explanation.surface: Ending a speech with a solemn-sounding film script.
explanation.definitionFit: A script is the written text of a film or play, here a screenplay.

clue.text: Race to put the carpet down again?

definitions.meaning: a team race in which runners hand over a baton

definitions.text: to put the carpet down again?
definitions.meaning: read as ..., to lay a carpet a second time

explanation.surface: A question about hurrying to refit a carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: A relay is a team race, and to re-lay is to lay again.

clue.text: Spring mist obscures riot beginning in children's game

parts.note: to spring is to leap

indicators.note: the mist covers over the letter, so it goes inside it

parts.note: fog is a thick mist

indicators.note: only the opening letter of riot is used

explanation.surface: A springtime fog hides the start of a riot during a playground game.
explanation.definitionFit: Leapfrog is a playground game in which children vault over each other's backs.

clue.text: Contributor doesn't have the heart to find a way out

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a donor is a contributor

explanation.surface: A heartless donor looks for an exit.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of DONOR is its middle letter, N.
explanation.definitionFit: A door is an exit, a way out of a room.

clue.text: Sick individual working to embrace America's fantasy

parts.note: ill means sick
US is the United States
I is one, a single individual
on means working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A sick person at work holds on to an American dream.
explanation.definitionFit: An illusion is a false idea or fantasy that does not match reality.

clue.text: One's promised to provide backing, one name having dropped out

indicators.note: the letter for name leaves the word, so it is removed

parts.note: to finance a project is to back it with money

explanation.surface: Someone promises to fund a venture after one backer withdraws.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiancé is a man engaged to be married, one who has been promised in marriage.

clue.text: Part of computer that's crucial to have on table

indicators.note: the second word is placed after the first, like something put on a table

parts.note: key means crucial, as in a key point
a board is a table, as in a festive board

explanation.surface: A computer component that is essential to keep on the desk.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard is the input device of a computer, one of its parts.

clue.text: Accepts a good wise man returning

indicators.note: the word for a wise man is read backwards

parts.note: a seer is a wise man or prophet

explanation.surface: A good sage comes back and accepts something.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree to something is to accept it.
